slices.label: Men outside the South
slices.source: 1860 census (Eighth Census), white men 21+ outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property tests had mostly ended, and only five New England states let Black men vote on equal terms; calibrated to certified returns.

slices.label: Women outside the South
slices.source: No women could vote for president in 1860; 1860 census women 21+ shown for population only.

slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1860 census, white adults in the eleven later-Confederate states; white men voted except in South Carolina, whose legislature chose its electors; the free-soil nominee was on no ballot in ten of these states; calibrated to certified returns.

slices.label: Black Southerners, most of them enslaved
slices.source: 1860 census, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote and no Southern state let free Black men vote.

slices.label: Immigrants not yet citizens
slices.source: 1860 census, foreign-born white men not yet naturalized; several Midwestern and Western states let declarant aliens vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.

whatIfs.label: Everyone Votes
whatIfs.detail: Every adult can vote, and turns out.
whatIfs.assumption: Every adult votes. Non-citizens choose like naturalized citizens of their state and sex; Black Southerners like Black voters outside the South; everyone else as their group did in 1860.

runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1860 comes out as it did: Lincoln wins, 172–0–123. The closest state was South Carolina, which went to Lincoln by 0.0 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1860 census counts and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1860 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.
